T: Three sisters, one cauldron, and the kids get first helpings.
D: Two Salem teenagers accidentally bring the Sanderson sisters back on Halloween night and have until sunrise to stop them.
P: Serve the snacks when Becca and Izzy light the black candle in the woods for Becca's birthday.
S: Winifred's spell book, with its one eye that never stops watching

Hard-boiled eggs filled with creamy mustard yolk, each with a black olive eye and a dusting of smoked paprika. Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water, then peel and halve lengthways. Mash the yolks with 3 tbsp mayonnaise and 1 tsp Dijon mustard and season well. Spoon or pipe the filling back into the whites. Press half a pitted black olive into the middle of each for an eye, dust with 1/2 tsp smoked paprika and scatter with chopped chives.
the Halloween festival filling Salem's town square

Frankfurts on sticks dipped in sweet polenta batter and fried golden, with tomato sauce and yellow mustard. Whisk 150g fine polenta, 150g plain flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp salt, then whisk in 1 egg and 250ml milk to a thick batter and pour into a tall glass. Heat 1.5 litres of vegetable oil in a deep heavy pan to 180C. Pat 8 frankfurts dry and push a bamboo skewer into each. Dip each in the batter and fry 2 or 3 at a time, turning, for about 3 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper towel and serve hot with tomato sauce and yellow mustard.
M: Winifred's cauldron beef and pumpkin stew with herb dumplings
the sisters' cauldron bubbling away in the old cottage

Slow-simmered beef with carrots and butternut pumpkin in a thick thyme gravy, with fluffy parsley dumplings steamed on top. Toss 1kg cubed beef chuck in 2 tbsp seasoned plain flour and brown in batches in 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot, then lift out. Soften 1 chopped brown onion, 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 carrots in the pot, stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, then add 1 litre beef stock, 2 bay leaves and 1 tsp dried thyme. Return the beef, cover and simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours. Add 600g butternut pumpkin chunks and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Rub 60g cold butter into 200g self-raising flour with 2 tbsp chopped parsley and a pinch of salt, stir in 150ml milk and roll into 8 balls. Sit them on the stew, cover and simmer for 20 minutes until puffed. Season and serve 2 dumplings to a bowl.
Becca's birthday pumpkin and sage mac and cheese
Becca's sixteenth, the night the Black Flame Candle gets lit

Macaroni baked in a roast pumpkin and cheddar sauce with crisp sage and a golden crumb top. Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the pumpkin in half the oil until soft, then mash. Boil the macaroni until just short of done and drain. Melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk until thick, then add the pumpkin and most of the cheddar. Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish and top with the rest of the cheddar, crumbs and sage leaves tossed in the last of the oil. Bake until golden.
W: the black candle Gilbert hands Becca for her birthday

Dark chocolate puddings baked until just set outside with a molten middle, with vanilla ice cream. Brush four 200ml pudding moulds with soft butter and dust with cocoa. Melt 100g chopped dark chocolate with 100g butter over simmering water and cool slightly. Whisk 2 eggs, 2 egg yolks and 60g caster sugar until thick and pale, fold in the chocolate, then 2 tbsp plain flour, and divide between the moulds. Chill for 30 minutes. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until risen with a soft wobble in the middle, stand for 1 minute, then turn out and serve with vanilla ice cream.
K: the glowing bottles on the shelves of Gilbert's magic shop

Bright green kiwi, apple and lime with bruised mint, topped with lemonade and frozen grape eyeballs. Blend 4 peeled kiwifruit with 500ml apple juice and the juice of 1 lime until smooth, then strain into a jug, pressing on the pulp. Bruise half a bunch of mint and stir it in. Fill 4 glasses with ice, pour in the green potion and top with 750ml lemonade. Garnish each glass with a skewer of 3 frozen green grapes, a lime wheel and a mint sprig.

dishes.n: Winifred's cauldron beef and pumpkin stew with herb dumplings
dishes.make_ahead: Make the stew up to 2 days ahead and chill; reheat until bubbling and add the dumplings on the night

steps.text: Toss the beef in the plain flour with salt and pepper and brown well in batches in the oil in a heavy pot. Lift out.
Cook the onion, garlic and carrots in the same pot until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the stock, bay leaves and thyme. Return the beef, cover and simmer gently until tender.
Add the pumpkin and simmer, uncovered, until just soft.
Meanwhile rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the parsley and a pinch of salt, stir in the milk to a soft dough and roll into 8 balls.
Sit the dumplings on top of the stew, cover and simmer until puffed and cooked through.
Season the stew and ladle into bowls with 2 dumplings each.

veg.n: Winifred's cauldron mushroom and pumpkin stew with herb dumplings
veg.make_ahead: Make the stew up to 2 days ahead and chill; reheat until bubbling and add the dumplings on the night

steps.text: Brown the mushrooms in batches in the oil in a heavy pot until dark, then lift out.
Cook the onion, garlic and carrots in the same pot until soft.
Stir in the plain flour and tomato paste, then the soy sauce, stock, bay leaves and thyme. Add the mushrooms, lentils and pumpkin and simmer, uncovered, until the pumpkin is soft.
Meanwhile rub the butter into the self-raising flour with the parsley and a pinch of salt, stir in the milk to a soft dough and roll into 8 balls.
Sit the dumplings on top of the stew, cover and simmer until puffed and cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper and ladle into bowls with 2 dumplings each.

Boil the macaroni until just short of done and drain.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk until thick, then add the pumpkin and most of the cheddar.
Fold in the pasta, tip into a dish and top with the rest of the cheddar, crumbs and sage leaves tossed in the last of the oil. Bake until golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Fill the moulds up to 1 day ahead and keep in the fridge; bake from cold for 1 to 2 minutes longer

steps.text: Brush four 200ml pudding moulds with the soft butter and dust with the cocoa.
Melt the chocolate and diced butter together in a bowl over simmering water, then cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until thick and pale.
Fold in the chocolate, then the flour, and divide between the moulds.
Chill until firm.
Heat the oven to 200C and bake on a tray until risen with a soft wobble in the middle.
Stand for 1 minute, turn out onto plates and serve with the ice cream.
